title: Finite errors and countable diagonalization

based_on.title: Combinatorial Set Theory: with a gentle introduction to forcing
based_on.pages: 190–192 (Chapter 8, definitions and Theorems 8.1 and 8.3; indexing and strict bound repaired)

summary: Countably many compatible requirements can be satisfied with finitely many exceptions.
abstract: The tails of the natural numbers have empty common intersection: no number lies beyond every cutoff. Nevertheless, the whole set of natural numbers is contained in each tail apart from finitely many exceptions. This phenomenon persists for any countable family of subsets whose finite intersections are infinite: an infinite approximate intersection always exists. Likewise, any countable family of functions from the natural numbers to themselves has a single function that exceeds each member at all sufficiently large inputs. The cutoff may depend on the member, which makes these conclusions possible.
